entries.text: What a way to go. Have you seen this m.o. Before, detective? Men cremated alive?

entries.text: Eleventh time, actually. There were three in Seattle, three in los angeles and two in boston. All chinese men between the ages of 20 and 40. All recent immigrants.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: We weren't able to determine any of that until just recently. The other two bodies were much more badly burned. We got lucky with this one.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: Lucky? That's an interesting word for it.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Got any leads on this case, detective? Any thoughts or ideas?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: We've got a big influx of immigrants from hong kong, trying to get out before 1997. And we've seen stepped up gang activity in the chinese community, but so far we can't tie these deaths to anyone or anything.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: You got anybody that can read or speak chinese?

entries.text: Yeah. Glen Chao. He's right over there. Why?

entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Does that mean anything to you?

entries.text: I don't know, but it's something strange for a man... Being burned alive to write, don't you think?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What's this? Anybody recognize this? Looks like some kind of foreign currency.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It's called "hell money." it's used as an offering during the chinese festival of the hungry ghosts.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: It's not money, per se. It's a symbolic offering to the evil spirits and the ghosts. For good luck.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Where would I get this "hell money?"
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, there aren't a whole lot of places in chinatown that sell it.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: That's good. Maybe we just found a way to identify the body.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: His name is johnny lo. He moved here about six months ago from canton. He's still in the I.n.s. Application process. He was a dishwasher in chinatown.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: How many dishes do you have to break before your boss tosses you in an oven?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I think it's pretty clear this is some kind of... A horrific cult or gang retribution killing.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Why would he write the character for ghost... On the inside of the crematory oven?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What about the guard seeing three figures that seemed to vanish without a trace?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Who you gonna call? Ghosts or ancestral spirits have been central... To chinese spiritual life for centuries.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: So you're saying the ancestral spirits... Pushed johnny lo into the oven and turned on the gas?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: That would sure teach him to respect his elders.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I checked all the neighboring buildings. Nobody saw or heard a thing. Not surprisingly.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: I don't recognize that. It could be idiomatic. Some kind of code.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Can you copy it down for me?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Someone's been here. This place has been cleaned out. Look at this.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yeah, that's what it looks like.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: What slumlord would spring for a new carpet in a dump like this?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Looks like they saved some money on carpet tacks... And didn't even bother replacing the old padding.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It's a dried frog. I think they're sometimes used as charms. Good health, prosperity, protection.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Looks like mr. Lo could've used a little of both. Let's get this blood tested.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I couldn't tell you what any one of these things are.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Well, they're roots mostly, like ginseng, turmeric. Then you got your more exotic stuff-- bear gall bladder, snake, shark fin-- usually prepared in a soup or a tea.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: What had the victim been using?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: She says that it's skullcap root and chinese angelica. They're used for painkillers.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Does she remember johnny lo or remember selling it to him?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Ask her if she knows he's dead.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Ask her if she recognizes those characters that were painted on his door.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: She says that the house was branded the tsang fang. A haunted house.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Yeah. It's hard to give it an exact translation, but it's what I was telling you about before. The chinese yu lan hui-- the festival of the hungry ghosts. You see, on the 15th day of the seventh moon... In the chinese calendar, it's believed the Gates of hell are opened... And the ghosts of unwanted souls roam the earth. Now, believers protect themselves by leaving gifts of food... And "hell money" outside their homes to appease the ghosts, to keep them from coming inside and causing trouble. But for some spirits, the ghosts most feared by the chinese, there's no buying them off.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: The preta, the ancient ghost of a murdered man... Who wanders the earth exacting his revenge on the living, or the wu chang keui, who collects the souls of doomed men and drags them down to... Ti yu-- to the chinese hell.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Think these murders could be related?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, it makes sense. This year's festival is just about over.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: What about you, detective? Do you believe in yu lan hui?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I find it hard to argue with 2,000 years of chinese belief, the stuff my parents and grandparents believe in. But the truth is, I'm more haunted by the size of my mortgage payments.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: The night patrolman described three men... Wearing the same masks as the ones ID'ed at the crematory.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: We don't know exactly. They were spotted around this grave over here, but we can't figure out exactly what they were up to.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: Yeah, there's a burial here at noon tomorrow.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: I don't know. We can check. Chao, see if you can get the name of the future occupant here.
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: I still don't understand what anybody would want with an empty grave.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Something just occurred to me. It looks like somebody was trying to get two burials for the price of one.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: A lot. And I haven't even finished my preliminary visual exam. Look at this. This guy's like a jigsaw puzzle. These are all surgical incisions. And judging by the color of the scars, I'd say... They were all made within the last year.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Do you know how much the human body is worth, Mulder?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Depends on the body. I don't know, a few bucks. How much?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: You're saying this guy was selling his body parts for money?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: A kidney, a portion of the liver, a cornea, bone marrow-- a person can lose these things and live to cash his social security checks.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: He won't be cashing any social security checks any time soon.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No, but if I'm right, this is one man who left his heart in san francisco.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Scully, even if you're right, it doesn't figure. There's no long-term business sense to dying. And what connection does this have to the crematory deaths?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: We only saw one body, but the only thing that wasn't burned to a delicate crisp... On johnny lo was his glass eye.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Maybe you can tell us. It was found in the body cavity of the man who was dumped in the grave.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: You said the frog was the symbol of luck and prosperity. Unless this is somebody's sick joke, I'd say it must have another meaning.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Well, if it does, I don't know what it is. I mean, it could be some kind of triad symbol, something from organized crime.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Well, maybe you can tell me this. Have you heard any word on the street about a black-market selling of body parts?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: This man with a frog in his chest was missing a cornea and a kidney. They were taken prior to the time of death, before the final removal of his heart, and I found what is known as sterile ice... On the skin in and around the incision on his chest. It is a substance used to preserve human organs for transplant.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't even know where to start.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Well, we're going to need more help from you than that, detective.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: The implication being that I'm not trying to help.
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: Either you resent us being here, or you feel some kind of protectiveness towards the chinese community.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Look, you don't even know what the hell you're dealing with here. This isn't some pretty little lacquer box... You can just take the lid off and find out what's inside. You might see the face of a chinese man here, but let me tell you something, they don't see the same face. They see the face of a cop. American-born chinese. A.b.c. To them, I'm just as white as you are. You think because I can speak the language, I can get all your answers for you. But what good is an interpreter when everyone speaks the language of silence?
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: It's the name of the company... That installed the carpet in johnny lo's apartment. I just happened to run across it while I was sitting there twiddling my thumbs. You coming or not?
entries.speaker: Detective Glen Chao

entries.text: I'm detective Chao with the san francisco police. Could we have a word with you?

entries.text: What was the name of the man who lived at this apartment?

entries.text: His name was johnny lo. He's dead now. Murdered. And we think that the carpet was laid in an attempt to cover up evidence. Your employer said you usually work as an apprentice.

entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't know any of this.
entries.speaker: Hsin Shih

entries.text: Thank you, mr. Hsin. If we need you, we'll get back to you. Thank you.

entries.text: I'm just a little tired and jumpy. One more string of firecrackers goes off, I'm gonna get out of the car and shoot somebody.

entries.text: Well, you can use the one down at st. Francis's hospital.

entries.text: Detective Chao was attacked in his town house tonight. I just talked to lieutenant Neary. He says he's cut up pretty bad.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't know, but we should check it out.

entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Wait a minute. What are you saying?
entries.speaker: Lieutenant Neary

entries.text: That the blood that we found on the carpet padding... In the victim's apartment was detective Chao's.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: And I'd be willing to bet that he's the one that asked for it to be installed.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: We're looking for mr. Hsin. Is he home?

entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Oh, I don't know. He goes out. I know he does for me-- because of me.

entries.text: Uh, I was diagnosed with... Acute lymphocytic leukemia six months ago.

entries.text: But in chinese it also correspond to the eye. Like fire to the heart and earth to the flesh.

entries.text: Hey, Scully. Look who's here. This must be the place after all.

entries.text: Chao, hands in the air! Hands in the air!

entries.text: He said... The game's not over.

entries.text: My people live with ghosts-- the ghosts of our fathers... And our fathers' fathers. They call to us from distant memory, showing us the path.

entries.text: No ghosts called to those men. You did, by preying on their hopelessness and their desperation.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yes. They were desperate. Just as I was desperate when I first came to this country. But I... Committed no crime.
entries.speaker: Hard-Faced Man

entries.text: You cheated them out of life... By promising them prosperity when the only possible reward was death.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: In my belief, death is nothing to be feared. It's merely a stage of transition. But life without hope, hmph, now that's living hell. So-- hope was my gift to these men.

entries.text: I don't expect you to understand.

entries.text: I understand this. You are going to prison for a very long time.

entries.text: Can I talk to you for a minute? I just got back from st. Francis hospital. Hsin's still in intensive care.

entries.text: It's our case against this guy. We've had our task force interviewing everybody we busted at the gaming parlor that night.
